newsitem.title: CANADA: Hydro-Quebec says not infiltrated by death cult.
newsitem.headline: Hydro-Quebec says not infiltrated by death cult.

text.p: Hydro-Quebec said on Friday that the Solar Temple death cult did not infiltrate the provincially owned utility, but the cult's deceased leader had been paid to give management courses to some employees.

Those were among the findings of an internal investigation into allegations by a former Hydro-Quebec employee that the Solar Temple had infiltrated the company and was blocking promotions for employees who were not members of the cult.
Hydro-Quebec generates and distributes most electrical power in the French-speaking province of 7.1 million people.
A 52-page report prepared by an advisory committee formed a year ago to investigate the allegations concluded the allegations were unfounded, Hydro-Quebec officials said.
"The report concludes that there was no infiltration," Hydro-Quebec Secretary General Marie-Jose Nadeau told a news conference.
The Solar Temple is an international cult whose members believe a ritualized death takes them on a journey to a new life on the star Sirius.
The report indicated that Hydro-Quebec paid C$7,500 ($5,475) to Solar Temple leader Luc Jouret for motivational courses offered to some of the utility's managerial staff.

Jouret is believed to have died in a group suicide by cult members in Switzerland in 1994. Since then, 74 cult members and others have been killed in group suicides and murders in Quebec, France and Switzerland.
A Hydro-Quebec vice-president and his wife died in the first set of group suicides.
In 1993, 15 Hydro-Quebec employees were members of the Solar Temple or the Academie de Recherche et de Connaissances des Hautes Etudes (ARCHS), a related group, the report said.
Hydro-Quebec Auditor General Daniel Lafleur said none of the company's 27,000 current employees were members of the Solar Temple or ARCHS.

But he said that two might be members of the Fondation du Graal, a group that received almost million C$1.5 million ($1.1 million) over nine years from Hydro-Quebec for management courses, some of which were of an "esoteric" nature.

Yves Casgrain, a Quebec cult investigator who helped prepare the report, said that while the Fondation du Graal was technically not a cult, it was "flagrant breach of ethics" for the Fondation to be offering courses to Hydro-Quebec staff.
